title: Karma Cannot Bind
author: Zhanran
excerpt: At the moment of death, karma cannot bind, and wherever one turns one is free.

inline.s: Cultivate the root with a sincere heart and right intention,
let not following a thought as it arises be the standard.
Take the self-nature as your essence; do not identify with the physical body;
take the numinous knowing as your own mind; do not identify with delusive thoughts.
When delusive thoughts arise, follow none of them,
then at the moment of death, karma cannot bind you, and wherever you turn you are free.
"All living beings are endowed with the nature of awakening, luminous, still, and void, in no way different from the Buddha. Only because,

from beginningless kalpas they have never awakened, deludedly clinging to the body as "self," they give rise to feelings of love and aversion. Following emotion they create karma; following karma they receive its retribution — birth, aging, sickness, and death, revolving for long kalpas. Yet the nature of awakening within the body has never known birth or death: as in a dream one is driven about, while the body itself is at ease; as water turns to ice, yet the wet nature does not change. If one can awaken to this nature

as the Dharma body, which of itself was never born — what need is there of reliance? Luminous and undimmed, ever clearly knowing, it has come from nowhere and goes nowhere. Still, the delusive clinging of many lives has become a habit of nature; joy, anger, sorrow, and pleasure flow in subtle streams. Though the true principle is suddenly reached, these emotions are hard to erase at once; one must constantly be aware, diminishing them again and again. As the wind suddenly stops and the waves gradually still — how could the cultivation of a single lifetime equal the power and function of the Buddhas? Only take emptiness and stillness as one's own essence, not identifying with the physical body; take the numinous knowing as one's own mind, not identifying with delusive thoughts.
When delusive thoughts arise, follow none of them
— then at the moment of death, karma of itself cannot bind.

Though there be an intermediate state, wherever one turns one is free; among gods or among humans, one may dwell at will. If the thoughts of love and aversion are already extinguished, one no longer receives the body of separate existence
(no more of the birth-and-death of separate existence)

, and of itself can exchange the short for the long, the coarse for the subtle. If the subtle streams all become still, and only the great wisdom of perfect awakening stands alone and luminous, then responding to conditions one manifests hundreds of billions of bodies to deliver living beings of karmic affinity — this is called being a Buddha."
Record of the Transmission of the Lamp)
